predecessors.name: Dai (Sixteen Kingdoms)
predecessors.text: Shengle and the Dai home belt, restored by Tuoba Gui in 386

successors.name: Eastern Wei
successors.text: Gao Huan's Eastern Wei, established 8 November 534

successors.name: Western Wei
successors.text: Yuwen Tai's Western Wei: Guanzhong and Gansu

ledger.x: 386: Tuoba Gui restores the state of Dai at Shengle and takes the name Wei.
396: Murong Chui leads a campaign against Wei and the Wei invade Later Yan.
397: Murong Bao abandons Zhongshan to the Wei.
398: the Wei hold most of Later Yan's land.
398: Tuoba Gui moves the capital from Shengle to Pingcheng.
398: the fighting for Hebei ends with Later Yan reduced to Longcheng and a Southern Yan at Huatai.
422: the Wei invade Liu Song.
423: the Wei take Luoyang, Xuchang and Hulao from Liu Song.
424: the Rouran invade the Wei.
426: the Wei go to war with Xia.
427: the Wei storm Tongwancheng and take Guanzhong from Xia.
430: Liu Song takes back Luoyang and Hulao.
430: the first Liu Song war ends in the Song recovery of the four cities; the next fighting the page records is 450.
431: the last Xia emperor falls.
431: Xia disestablished.
432: Wei attacks on Northern Yan begin.
433: Feng Hong's sons hand Liaoxi Commandery to Wei.
434: the Rouran and Wei make a marriage alliance.
436: the Wei conquer Northern Yan.
436: Northern Yan ends.
439: Emperor Taiwu conquers Northern Liang.
441: the last Juqu seats in western Hexi fall.
443: the Wei attack the Rouran again.
450: Emperor Wen of Liu Song invades the Wei; the Wei counter-invade.
451: the Wei troops withdraw from the south in January.
458: the last Wei attack on the Rouran that the page dates.
466: Liu Song's northern governors defect to Wei after the Liu Zixun rising.
466: Xue Andu surrenders Xu Province to the Wei.
468: Murong Baiyao takes Qing and Ji Provinces.
468: the Liu Song north-east is Wei land.
493: Emperor Xiaowen moves the capital from Pingcheng to Luoyang.
505: Hanzhong and Xinyang fall to the Wei.
523: the Six Garrisons on the northern frontier rise.
525: the Poliuhan Baling rebellion is defeated.
534: the western half becomes the Western Wei.
534: the Northern Wei dissolves into the Eastern and Western Wei.
534: Gao Huan installs Yuan Shanjian as ruler of Eastern Wei.

wars.name: Northern Wei-Later Yan war
wars.outcome: Wei victory at Canhe Slope (8 December 395); Zhongshan evacuated 27 April 397; by 398 the Wei held most of Later Yan's land and Later Yan was left at Longcheng.

wars.name: Battle of Chaibi
wars.outcome: Later Qin suffered "a heavy defeat to the Northern Wei at the Battle of Chaibi in 402", which halted its eastward expansion; no land change is on the pages.

wars.name: Wei-Rouran wars
wars.outcome: Rouran invasion repulsed (424), Wei offensive (429), marriage alliance (434), Wei attacks 443, 449 (Rouran defeated), 456, 458; a 492 expedition of 70,000 horsemen with an unrecorded result.

wars.name: Wei-Liu Song war of 422-430
wars.outcome: Wei took Luoyang, Xuchang (spring 423), Hulao (summer 423), Sizhou and Yanzhou; in 430 Liu Song recovered Luoyang, Hulao, Huatai and Qiao'ao.

wars.name: Wei conquest of Xia
wars.outcome: Tongwancheng fell 11 July 427, Helian Chang was captured in 428, Helian Ding was captured by the Tuyuhun in 431 and handed to Wei.

wars.name: Wei conquest of Northern Yan
wars.outcome: Periodic attacks from 432; Liaoxi handed over in 433; a major invasion in 436 ended the state and Feng Hong fled to Goguryeo (executed 438).

wars.name: Wei conquest of Northern Liang
wars.outcome: Guzang besieged and Juqu Mujian surrendered in 439; the Juqu remnant held Jiuquan and Dunhuang to 442 and then Gaochang until the Rouran destroyed it in 460.

wars.name: Liu Song-Wei war of 450-451
wars.outcome: Emperor Wen's invasion was flanked and destroyed; the Liu Song provinces south of the Yellow River were devastated, only Huatai held out, and the Wei withdrew in January 451.

wars.name: Wei annexation of the Liu Song north-east
wars.outcome: Xu and Yan defected 466, Liu Song efforts to recover them failed in 467, Qing and Ji were annexed in spring 468.

wars.name: Wei-Southern Qi war
wars.outcome: "479: Wei prepared to invade Southern Qi, and fighting continued until 481"; a peace treaty was signed with Emperor Wu of Southern Qi in 490.

wars.name: Wei-Liang war of 503-505
wars.outcome: By spring 505 Xinyang and Hanzhong had fallen to Wei.

wars.name: Six Garrisons revolt
wars.outcome: The Poliuhan Baling rebellion was defeated in 525; Rouran forces helped suppress rebels 525-527; Erzhu Rong's massacre at Heyin (17 May 528) and the split of 534 followed.

certainty.note: Every frontier is approximate: the steppe frontier with the Rouran, the Tuyuhun and Gaochang frontier, the Huai-Yellow River frontier with Liu Song, Southern Qi and Liang.
